## Failure mode

Strict Snap Chromium can exit **0** while failing to write a screenshot to a host
`/tmp` path. The browser runs in a private mount namespace, so the host directory
exists for the shell but is absent from Chromium's view. The only useful signal is
stderr:

```text
Failed to write file /tmp/.../shot.png: No such file or directory (2)
```

Do not treat Chromium's exit status, or a command that merely printed a path, as
evidence that the PNG exists.

## Safe capture recipe

Use a non-hidden, persistent directory under `$HOME`. The Snap home interface can
see this path, while host `/tmp` is not reliable for Snap output:

```sh
set -euo pipefail

CHROMIUM_BIN=${CHROMIUM_BIN:-/snap/bin/chromium}
SCREENSHOT_ROOT=${PAPERCUSP_CHROMIUM_SCREENSHOT_DIR:-"$HOME/papercusp-chromium-screenshots"}
mkdir -p "$SCREENSHOT_ROOT"
RUN_DIR="$(mktemp -d "$SCREENSHOT_ROOT/run.XXXXXX")"
OUT="$RUN_DIR/shot.png"
URL=${1:?pass the URL or file:// URL to capture}

"$CHROMIUM_BIN" \
  --headless=new \
  --disable-gpu \
  --window-size=1440,900 \
  --screenshot="$OUT" \
  "$URL" >"$RUN_DIR/stdout.log" 2>"$RUN_DIR/stderr.log"

test -s "$OUT" || {
  echo "Screenshot was not created: $OUT" >&2
  cat "$RUN_DIR/stderr.log" >&2
  exit 1
}

test "$(head -c 8 "$OUT" | od -An -t x1 | tr -d ' \\n')" = \
  89504e470d0a1a0a || {
  echo "Screenshot is not a PNG: $OUT" >&2
  exit 1
}

npm run check:screenshot -- "$OUT"
echo "Screenshot: $OUT"
```

The output directory is intentionally not under `/tmp`; `RUN_DIR` preserves the
PNG and Chromium logs for review. Set
`PAPERCUSP_CHROMIUM_SCREENSHOT_DIR` when the home directory is not the desired
evidence location.

## Verification rule

A successful command needs all three checks: Chromium completed, stderr was retained
for diagnosis, and `test -s "$OUT"` passed. Then run
`npm run check:screenshot -- "$OUT"` so a valid-but-blank capture is rejected.
If stderr contains `Failed to write file` or the output check fails, recapture to the
persistent home path; never cite the missing path as visual evidence.
